source_refs.note: Wheat Grain Colour: a main subheading of 18.5.1 Polygenic Inheritance, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 98-98.

blocks.text: Wheat grain colour shows continuous variation, ranging from white to dark red. This trait is controlled by three polygenes: A, B, and C. Each gene has a dominant allele (A, B, C) that produces red pigment and a recessive allele (a, b, c) that does not. The genotype AABBCC produces the maximum red pigment, so the grains are dark red. In contrast, aabbcc produces no pigment, so the grains are white. See the following cross.

When dark red wheat (AABBCC) is crossed with white wheat (aabbcc), the F1 generation (AaBbCc) shows an intermediate red colour. In the F2 generation, during crossbreeding, a wide range of colours appears. Only one plant will darkest red grains (AABBCC) and one will plant will have white grains. While 62 plants will show different shades of red (moderate red to very light red).

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Environmental factors like light, water and nutrients also influence the grain colour.
